subject: Streaming reliability in polyfilled browsers — SDK workaround + triage
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@brightlane.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: streaming responses missing partial chunks in our web client

Hey Avery —

We're seeing intermittent missing chunks when using Redwood's streaming endpoint from our Electron/web wrapper that uses a fetch polyfill. The stream completes but the last 20-40% of streaming content is never emitted to our onmessage handler. This only reproduces in our packaged app (Chromium 100-ish + fetch polyfill) — works fine in Chrome proper.

Repro steps (short):
- Call /v1/streams with model=X and streaming=true
- Use fetch polyfill (whatwg-fetch) inside our wrapper
- Sometimes the server sends responses (we see network-level) but the client never receives final chunk(s)

Attached: brightlane_stream.log (client-side logs) and a short runbook. Can someone from Redwood confirm if this is a known behavior or a bug in SDK/runtime? This is blocking our demo next Wednesday (10/20).

Thanks — Sam
Sam Park
Head of Integrations, Brightlane

Looping platform/runtime and PM. Sam from Brightlane reports intermittent truncated streams when their app uses a fetch polyfill. They attached client logs — brightlane_stream.log (see attachment).

Why this matters: Brightlane has a vendor demo scheduled 10/20; we need a short-term workaround (SDK or config) and a triage plan for a proper fix.

Quick context / what I tried: I asked Eng to repro locally with Electron 100 and their repro.sh (they shared a simple repro command). I couldn't repro in Chrome.

Ask for Platform/Runtime:

- Short-term: can we ship an SDK flag to force chunked transfer semantics or change client-side buffering?
- Long-term: root cause + runtime fix timeline and canary plan.

Attaching their repro.sh that Sam sent. I'll coordinate customer comms once we have a timeline.

—Avery

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: streaming responses missing partial chunks in our web client

Thanks for the reproduction and logs, Avery. I pulled the brightlane_stream.log and ran their repro.sh in an Electron 100 container and verified behavior aligns with what Sam described. Notes below.

Summary of findings so far:
- At the transport layer the server emits the full chunk sequence (we see all chunk frames in tcpdump).
- The Redwood runtime is streaming and not closing the connection early.
- The polyfilled fetch implementation in Electron appears to buffer until a content-length or explicit end-of-stream signal is received; some intermediate flushes are not delivered to the app event loop.
- Likely interaction: our current streaming path uses implicit chunk flushing behavior that browsers rely on; polyfills that reimplement fetch/readable-stream can collapse or coalesce chunks.

Immediate mitigation options (short-term):
1) SDK-level opt-in header: X-Redwood-Force-Chunked: true — instructs runtime to send explicit small chunk frames and repeated flush boundaries. We can add support in the JS SDK quickly (patch in ~1 day) to set header when user passes streamingPolyfillWorkaround: true.
2) Server-side: force explicit chunk boundary markers and heartbeat chunks for streaming sessions from runtime — requires a runtime change, low-risk but needs rollout. ETA: can do a canary within 1 week, full rollout 2–3 weeks depending on validation.

Proposed action plan:
- Today: I will prepare an SDK patch (sdk-patch.diff) that exposes streamingPolyfillWorkaround and sets X-Redwood-Force-Chunked. Patch ready EOD. (Attached stub.)
- Tomorrow: coordinate with infra to enable a canary server-side toggle that forces extra flushes for sessions that present the header. Canary target: a single region/ASG. ETA for canary: 2026-10-15.
- 10/22: plan runtime change rollout if canary metrics look good.

Risks/notes:
- Extra flushes increase token echo + egress by a small factor; need to call out cost impact to customer.
- We should document guidance for customers using polyfilled fetch/RN/Electron to opt-in to the workaround.

I'll follow up with a short RFC in the #runtime channel with telemetry we’ll collect.

—Dev

Subject: Re: Quick: streaming responses missing partial chunks in our web client

Sam — quick update and next steps. Appreciate the repro and logs. Internal triage indicates this is an interaction between your fetch polyfill and how streaming flushes are coalesced.

What we'll do next:
- Today (10/15): we'll ship a JS SDK hotfix behind an opt-in flag (streamingPolyfillWorkaround). If you use the patched SDK and set streamingPolyfillWorkaround=true, the SDK will add header X-Redwood-Force-Chunked and the runtime will enable extra flushes for that session. Patch attached for tracking (sdk-patch.diff).
- Tomorrow (10/16): we'll enable a canary in us-west for sessions that present that header so you can validate in your staging Electron build.
- Target full runtime rollout: week of 10/22 if canary telemetry looks good.

Could you please confirm you can test the staging canary on 10/16 and share a quick repro checklist? We'll also include a short note on the expected slight increase in bytes and how to disable the workaround after full fix.

Thanks — will follow up with a short customer-facing blurb for your demo comms.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
